thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Incident detected — p99 latency spike on streaming/text-gen endpoints in eu-west-1. Alerts: p95 ~ 850ms (↑), p99 ~ 5.8s (breach). Suspected: ingress-egress policy imbalance + zone weight skew. Paging on-call.
morgan: seeing a big cluster of stalled streaming sessions, looks like streaming stalls during chunk flush. UI metrics show increased queueing at router level.
sandeep: @morgan can you paste the router logs for one of the stalled requests? want to check misroute/handoff traces.
morgan: grabbing logs, one example: `req=abc123 route=ingress-v2 -> egress-split(zone-b) handoff=timeout=3.0s backend=kvcache-hotshard`
chris: incoming from synthetic canaries too? or only real traffic?
morgan: canaries show degraded p99 as well starting ~1927502000 (10m ago). so replication.
kara: impact: Production customers in EU might see streaming stalls and early disconnects. No error spike (200s still common), but long tail responses.
maria: any recent config changes to routing/policies? I didn't see a deploy but infra did a policy rollout yesterday.
sandeep: yes there was a staged rollout of new ingress-egress split policy to spread load across zones. Looks like weight balancing is off for eu-west-1 (zone B got >60% traffic but has fewer warm warmups for hot shards).
oncall-bot: @oncall-eng assigned to this incident: morgan. Severity: Sev2. Please confirm.
morgan: acknowledged. I'm on it.
chris: quick ask — can we throttle new streaming sessions to protect existing ones while we triage?
sandeep: we can temporarily lower the ingress split weight for zone-b and increase fallback-to-zone-a. rolling change via routing service.
morgan: executing small mitigation: changing split weights now.
morgan: ```
# reduce weight to zone-b
curl -X POST "https://controlplane/api/route-adjust" -d '{"policy":"ingress-egress-split","zone_weights":{"a":0.6,"b":0.3,"c":0.1}}'
```
incident-bot: Route-adjust request accepted (change-id: rd-1927502475). Propagating.
maria: after the change, p99 dropped from 5.8s -> 1.8s in 90s. p95 back to ~400-600ms. Good signal.
kara: we should still investigate root cause — why zone-b got hot. Hot partitioning? failed pre-warm? cache skew?
sandeep: prelim traces show many requests to hotkeys are landing in zone-b due to egress-hash policy + new ingress split causing path skew. hot shard placement + fallback churn created queuing at the egress proxies.
chris: any evidence of misrouting where requests bounce between zones causing KV cache misses? That would explain stalls.
morgan: yes, see repeated handoffs with small TTL: `handoff_count=3` and `kvcache_miss=true` in logs for stalled sessions. TTL for pinned routes seems low.
sandeep: policy bug hypothesis: ingress-egress split didn't include affinity preservation for streaming pins — so streaming sessions could be routed to a different egress zone mid-session. That breaks KV cache locality.
maria: can we enforce session affinity for streaming as quick fix?
sandeep: yes, we can flip `streaming_affinity=true` on the policy for the affected prefix. Doing a controlled toggle.
morgan: toggled streaming_affinity=true for prefix `/v1/stream` on eu-west-1. Change-id rd-1927502498.
oncall-bot: Alert: change deployed to 3/3 routers in eu-west-1. Monitoring metrics.
maria: p99 dropped further to ~700ms in 2m. streaming stalls gone from being consistent to occasional. good.
kara: we should prepare a customer-facing note if p99 goes above threshold again. Any customers impacted so far?
morgan: support flagged two customer sessions that disconnected — I'll collect session IDs. No large-scale outages, more degraded quality.
chris: follow-ups: 1) root cause RCA planned, 2) revert or patch policy rollout to include affinity preservation, 3) add canary checks for affinity breaks, 4) longer term: warmup strategy for new zone weights.
sandeep: agree. I'll open a tracking issue and revert the staged rollout for now.
morgan: checking router-level telemetry for queue depths — before changes queue_len peaked ~48, after weight change and affinity toggle queue_len ~6-8.
maria: is there any risk with keeping affinity on? e.g., imbalance long-term if zone health degrades.
sandeep: it's a tradeoff. We'll keep affinity temporarily while we re-evaluate load placement and pre-warm heuristics.
kara: do we want to evict hot shards from zone-b to avoid re-queuing while warmup finishes?
chris: we can trigger a controlled drain of the worst-affected egress proxies (drain with no new session allocation) and bounce them after cache reset.
morgan: starting drain of egress-proxy-32 in zone-b. command:
```bash
controlplane drain egress-proxy-32 --mode=gradual --no-new-sessions
```
incident-bot: egress-proxy-32 drain initiated. ETA ~4m to reach zero active sessions.
maria: ops note: we also need to adjust alerts so that a policy rollout that changes zone weight by >10% triggers a canary test for session affinity and cache miss-rate.
sandeep: noted. I’ll add a policy gating check in the rollout pipeline.
chris: long-term items for RFC: - affinity-preserving ingress-egress split, - prewarm hot keys on weight changes, - per-prefix affinity opt-outs, - better telemetry on handoff_count and kvcache-miss.
kara: can someone draft a short status for customers and leadership summarizing mitigation + next steps?
morgan: writing a quick postmortem stub to the incidents tracker and will DM support with affected session IDs.
maria: production status: p99 stable ~650-900ms, p95 ~350-500ms. We'll keep monitoring for 60m before declaring mitigated.
oncall-bot: Incident status changed to "Mitigated" at 1927502805 by morgan. Please follow up with RCA.
morgan: oncall handoff in 10m to @sandeep for RCA; leaving notes in pager duty. Thanks all for quick responses.
sandeep: I'll take lead on RCA and follow-up work items. Will schedule 1h post-incident review in #eng-runtime.
chris: FYI I'll file the rollout revert PR and include tests for affinity.
maria: thanks everyone. I'll coordinate customer comms after we have RCA draft.
kara: :thumbsup: Good mitigation. Keep the thread updated if p99 creeps up again.
morgan: closing thread for active mitigation. will reopen if metrics degrade.
